title: ‘They were told bikes were for men’: how Latin America’s city of cycling is breaking gender barriers

paragraphs.en: Eliana González has a busy morning ahead of her, dropping off her son at school and picking up groceries. Her trusted vehicle to get around in Bogotá is a colourful cargo bike, adapted to carry her two children and occasionally her dog.
paragraphs.zh: 埃利安娜·冈萨雷斯（Eliana González）今天上午很忙：要送儿子上学，还要采购食品杂货。她在波哥大出行信赖的交通工具是一辆色彩鲜艳的货运自行车，经过改装可载她的两个孩子，偶尔还能带上她的狗。

paragraphs.en: “For me, my cargo bike is a way to carry my children safely and comfortably without polluting the environment,” she says.
paragraphs.zh: 她说：“对我来说，货运自行车是一种安全舒适地接送孩子、又不污染环境的方式。”

paragraphs.en: Widely regarded as a global cycling success story, the Colombian city of 10 million people records nearly 900,000 bicycle trips each day – more than any other city in Latin America.
paragraphs.zh: 这座拥有1000万人口的哥伦比亚城市被广泛视为全球自行车出行的成功典范，每天记录的自行车出行近90万次，超过拉丁美洲任何其他城市。

paragraphs.en: Now, city officials are working towards another milestone: achieving gender parity in cycling by 2039. Women accounted for only 28% of Bogotá’s daily bicycle trips in 2023, according to the city’s latest mobility survey . “Our goal is to move from a [nearly] 30–70 split to 50–50 parity,” says Claudia Díaz, Bogotá’s secretary of mobility.
paragraphs.zh: 如今，市政府官员正朝着另一个里程碑迈进：到2039年实现骑行的性别平等。根据该市最新的出行调查，2023年波哥大每日自行车出行中女性仅占28%。波哥大交通局长克劳迪娅·迪亚斯（Claudia Díaz）说：“我们的目标是从（近乎）3比7的比例转变为50比50的平等。”

paragraphs.en: Closing the gender gap makes for a more inclusive city, but also brings environmental benefits. Transportation is Bogotá’s largest source of greenhouse emissions , and officials say that boosting the number of female cyclists could support the capital’s goal of becoming carbon neutral by 2050 .
paragraphs.zh: 缩小性别差距不仅能让城市更具包容性，还能带来环境效益。交通是波哥大温室气体排放的最大来源，官员们表示，增加女性骑车人数可支持首都到2050年实现碳中和的目标。

paragraphs.en: “The challenge we face is how to increase the number of cycling trips,” says Díaz. “The more we increase the number of cycling trips, the more environmental benefits we see for our city.”
paragraphs.zh: 迪亚斯说：“我们面临的挑战是如何增加自行车出行次数。自行车出行次数增加得越多，我们城市获得的环境效益就越大。”

paragraphs.en: Experts say gender equality is essential for cities to fully realise the benefits of investing in sustainable transportation, which can lead to lower greenhouse gas emissions, cleaner air and reduced traffic congestion.
paragraphs.zh: 专家表示，要让城市充分实现可持续交通投资带来的好处（包括降低温室气体排放、改善空气质量和减少交通拥堵），性别平等至关重要。

paragraphs.en: “Those impacts aren’t really going to happen if only half the population is ever going to use that [transport] system,” says Dana Yanocha, a senior manager at the Institute for Transportation and Development Policy, a nonprofit organisation promoting sustainable transport.
paragraphs.zh: “如果只有一半的人口会使用（交通）系统，那么这些影响就不会真正实现，”推广可持续交通的非营利组织交通与发展政策研究所的高级经理达娜·亚诺查（Dana Yanocha）说。
